h: T. rex, Romans and a trip to the stars
p: Ask most kids what they remember from the Great North Museum and the answer is usually the T. rex. A full-size cast of the skeleton towers over visitors, and it is a guaranteed jaw-dropper. Nearby, galleries packed with animal specimens, from huge mammals to tiny insects, keep young naturalists busy.

The Hadrian's Wall gallery is a highlight for older visitors, with a big model of the wall and plenty of objects from the Roman frontier. It is a brilliant warm-up if you are planning to visit the wall itself, and a great way to understand why it mattered so much to this part of the world.

Don't miss the ancient Egyptian galleries, with real mummies and coffins, or the Greek and Roman collections. There is a planetarium too, with shows that take you on a trip across the night sky. Check the programme when you arrive, as planetarium shows are often ticketed separately.
Allow two or three hours to see it properly, though with younger children you might prefer to focus on a few favourite galleries and come back another time.

Nearby, the Hatton Gallery is on the university campus, while the Laing Art Gallery and the Discovery Museum are both within easy reach in the city centre. Grey's Monument and the elegant Grainger Town streets are a short walk away. To see the real Roman wall, hop on the Metro to Wallsend, where Segedunum Roman Fort marks the eastern end of Hadrian's Wall.
